what.text: This page follows refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina living in the United States, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 86 refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina in the United States, 0.3% of all refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Serbia and Kosovo is the largest host of refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by France and Denmark.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflicts in Bosnia-Herzegovina from 1992 to 1995, over Serb, Croat and Bihaca Krajina territory.
The main years of displacement in the data, 1998 to 2003 and 2006, come after those conflicts ended.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1993 at 1887 refugees.
The figure was at its highest, 114615, at the end of 2006, and has fallen since then.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
These are year-end totals for the United States only, reported to UNHCR.
